subject: Lantern Health - burst credit / SLO exception request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Lantern Health - request: burst credit escrow / SLO exception for go-live

Monica, Ben, Laura —

Quick context: Lantern Health is contract-signing today for a Tier-1 EHR integration (see attached MAP). They have a hard go-live on 2027-05-17 and are asking for a short-term guarantee we can sustain occasional 5–7x burst traffic for ~10 minutes, up to 3 times/day, for the first 30 days post-launch. Their procurement team also asked whether we can escrow "burst credits" so that their peak bursts do not immediately blow past committed throughput charges.

As discussed in the demo, Lantern will be sensitive to latency during peak hours. They're willing to accept a slightly relaxed 95th percentile SLO for those bursts if we provide explicit burst accounting and transparent token billing for burst windows. They are asking us to:

- Provide a documented burst-capability plan (what we'd do during bursts)
- Allow an escrowed pool of burst credits (prepaid or contractual) that can be consumed without immediate overage billing
- Confirm whether we can surface per-tenant burst telemetry to Lantern and to our billing system

Need: a product / eng assessment and one of the following outcomes this week:
A) We can commit to a short-term, contract-backed burst-credit escrow + telemetry, with a delivery plan and engineering ETA; or
B) We provide a clear fallback + pricing workaround (manual pre-warm + soft-priority queue) that Lantern accepts.

Attached: LH-MAP-v3.pdf (mutual action plan), and a short note from Lantern procurement.

I know this is tight — please flag blockers so I can manage expectations with Lantern.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

--

Subject: Re: Lantern Health - request: burst credit escrow / SLO exception for go-live

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads-up and the MAP. A few clarifying Qs before we scope engineering work:

1) Burst profile: can you share the expected baseline QPS and the concrete expected burst QPS (peak). Lantern's ask of 5–7x is broad; need absolute numbers to estimate capacity and cost.
2) Duration and frequency: you mentioned ~10 minutes, up to 3 times/day — do they expect these bursts to occur across multiple regions or one primary region (US-West)?
3) Escrow commercial model: will Lantern prepay a burst pool or do they expect a contractual buffer we invoice later? Finance will need the answer to draft a concession.
4) Telemetry / compliance: Lantern asked for per-tenant burst telemetry into their SIEM. Is that strictly an export of existing metrics or will we need to create a new trace-level export (possible PII concerns)?

From a product perspective, options are: (a) a config-level "burst-credit" mode that lifts rate limits for a tenant and decrements credits (requires backend billing hook + telemetry), (b) a prioritized-queue approach where latency-sensitive traffic gets higher priority up to a cap, or (c) short-lived dedicated capacity allocation (warm nodes) for the first 30 days. Each has different engineering effort and risk.

Ben — can you comment on perf implications and a rough lead time for (a) vs (b)/(c)? Laura — any CS/ops runbook we should prepare so the customer feels covered?

If we're to commit to anything in the contract this week, I need an engineering ETA + a short-risk statement.

—Monica
Group PM, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Lantern Health - request: burst credit escrow / SLO exception for go-live

Folks —

Thanks for laying this out. High-level feasibility and tradeoffs below. I also attached a short spec (burst_credit_spec_draft.md) with the implementation sketch.

Assumptions (will refine with exact QPS numbers): baseline tenant QPS = 25 r/s, requested burst = up to 150 r/s (6x), bursts last up to 10 minutes, up to 3/day.

Options:
1) "Burst-credit" escrow (recommended if customer prepays):
   - Mechanism: Token-based credits per tenant; when a tenant enters burst window, credit counter decrements and we lift conservative per-tenant throttles.
   - Engineering work: billing hook + quota-service change + UI flag + telemetry export.
   - Risk: moderate — touches billing and quota plumbing; needs careful testing (8–9 dev-weeks, functional + perf testing).

2) Prioritized soft-queue (fastest short-term):
   - Mechanism: Route traffic to priority queue for the tenant; background traffic gets deprioritized rather than hard denying. No billing change required initially.
   - Engineering work: routing rule + queue adjustments + canary config (2 dev-weeks).
   - Risk: low to medium — doesn't solve billing/escrow, but buys time for (1).

3) Short-lived dedicated warm pool (operational workaround):
   - Mechanism: Spin up dedicated warm nodes for Lantern for first 30 days. Fixed cost, predictable latency.
   - Engineering/ops: provisioning + autoscaler whitelist + runbook (3–4 ops-days).
   - Risk: low operational complexity, higher cost to Redwood.

Telemetry/Compliance: per-tenant metrics export is feasible via our metrics pipeline; depends on required granularity. Exporting trace-level details into Lantern's SIEM will need PII/PHI review — assumes Lantern signs a DPA amendment.

Recommendation: for contract signing this week, offer a two-part commitment:
- Short-term: Prioritized soft-queue + ops standby to pre-warm nodes (deliverable within 10 business days). This mitigates immediate risk with minimal platform change.
- Mid-term: Work on a burst-credit escrow feature (Option 1) as a 6–9 week project. Provide Lantern a roadmap and milestone dates; tie the feature to a paid add-on that covers engineering cost.

I'll queue up the initial canary config and a runbook; estimate to have a workable soft-queue + pre-warm ops runbook ready by 2027-05-14. If we get exact QPS numbers and confirmation on commercial model (prepay vs invoice), I can firm the timeline for the escrow feature.

—Ben
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: burst_credit_spec_draft.md (text/markdown)

Thanks for the quick decision on signature. To keep the go-live intact, here's what Redwood can commit to today:

1) Short-term operational mitigation (deliverable by 2027-05-14):
   - Implement a prioritized soft-queue for Lantern traffic and hold an ops standby to spin up dedicated warm nodes if we observe sustained degradation. This addresses latency risk while we scope the product feature.

2) Mid-term product work (target 6–9 weeks):
   - We will scope and deliver a formal "burst-credit escrow" product that allows prepaid burst pools and integrates with billing/telemetry. Ben's team will provide a roadmap and milestone schedule by 2027-05-07.

Action items for Lantern:
- Please confirm baseline QPS and expected peak QPS for the bursts (absolute numbers) by EOD 2027-05-05.
- Procurement: confirm whether you prefer prepay or invoice model for the burst pool so finance can draft commercial terms.
- Legal: if Lantern requires per-tenant trace export to SIEM, please flag DPA/PHI requirements.

Monica/Ben/Laura — I will notify Lantern that we will proceed with the short-term mitigation and provide Ben's runbook on 2027-05-14. I'll loop in Finance/Legal separately for the commercial amendment.

Jonas
